headline: MGAT Alpha closed just 2 trades this week for +$24.41 (1 winner, both in the BC family), but this report only covers about 44% of the week: no new trading data has arrived since 2026-10-06T22:29 UTC, so everything after that point - roughly three and a half days, including a mid-week code update that opens a new, not-yet-measured segment - is not in these numbers. The hold-benchmark comparison is withheld this week rather than published on a stale read: the only price snapshot available predates the week's own Saturday close. With the sample this thin and over half the week unobserved, no trading verdict is issued - the open issue this week is the missing data, not the trading logic.

counterfactual.reason: The shadow comparison book is void for this run: it could never close a position, so none of its figures measure anything.

llm_adviser: LLM adviser: observer only - logs what it would do, cannot affect a trade (settled from source 2026-09-22).
sample_caveat: 2 closed trades this week, 71 all-time against the 200-trade target (about 35%). 71 is past the floor where all-time win rate and PnL become directional rather than unreadable, but this week's own 2 trades - both in the same family, both on stand-in sizing rather than measured sizing, and drawn from under half the week - are not a read on their own.
paper_caveat: Alpha is paper - simulated fills, no slippage, no thin-liquidity exits, no can't-sell-into-dust. A clean logic result here is never a claim that the execution floor works; that claim belongs to the Beta rung alone.
integrity: A code change landed partway through this week (2026-10-07) that the project classes as its most significant tier of change - this week is a new segment under the standing segmentation rule and is not cleanly comparable to the week before it. Every trade in this report happened before that change.

verdict.text: Insufficient sample to call - in the data, not necessarily in the trading logic. The snapshot that feeds this report stopped updating four days before the week ended, so only 2 trades and under half the week's cycles are visible; a mid-week change the project classes as its largest tier also opened a new, not-yet-measured segment inside this same window. What is visible is unremarkable on its own: one profitable exit, one roughly break-even exit, a quiet run of regime readings, and no fault alarms. The one standing signal that still carries weight is the hold-benchmark comparison from the prior week, which had the book modestly behind simply holding its starting coins - this week's own comparison could not be published because the only available price read predates the week's close. Until the missing days are backfilled, no call on the trading logic itself is supportable.
